title: Affinity shed mitigation and hosted fallback circuitry for dedicated routing
creator: Aisha Patel
description: When dedicated capacity unexpectedly sheds affinity (slot reclamation, preemption or host-level failures) we need a deterministic, observable, and priority-aware fallback circuit to hosted variants that preserves SLOs for high-tier tenants while preventing cascade failures. This ticket designs and implements a conservative fallback 'circuitry' that: 1) detects affinity shedding events quickly, 2) computes a per-tenant stabilization window and priority-adjusted spillover budget, 3) selects compatible hosted model variants with degradation bounds, and 4) exposes controls and telemetry for operations and product teams.
acceptance_criteria: A monitoring alert is created that fires within 10s of a dedicated affinity shed event and surfaces tenant, shard, and slot metadata.
Fallback selection chooses hosted variant within configured compatibility matrix and enforces per-tenant spill budget and rate limit.
Rollout respects a stabilization window per tenant that prevents immediate re-eviction back to dedicated for at least the configured grace period.
Circuit breaker prevents more than 5% of total requests for a region from spilling to hosted during sustained degradation (configurable), with automatic dampening after 5 minutes.
End-to-end tests (integration) simulate preemption, eviction, and region-wide saturation and show fallbacks degrade gracefully without exceeding token-cost guardrails.
Operational playbook added to runbook.md and Console dashboard surface points-of-failure and tenant-level spill metrics.
PRs implementing runtime routing logic and console telemetry are merged and reviewed by Runtime and Observability teams.
progress_updates: 2025-02-11: Initial design draft posted to Confluence (doc: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/RI/affinity-shed-fallback) with two proposed algorithms (budgeted-rate vs weighted-probabilistic).

2025-02-13: Architecture sync with Runtime and Observability — agreed to start with budgeted-rate approach for predictable unit-economics. Follow-up: proof-of-concept for per-tenant budgets (ENG-87022-POC branch).

2025-02-15: POC implemented for budgeted-rate fallback in staging; observed spike in hosted latency when naive spillover allowed >10% of region traffic. Added per-region dampening and global cap prototype.
2025-02-17: Safety feature: stabilization windows added (default 60s) to avoid flip-flopping between dedicated and hosted. Integration tests updated.

2025-02-19: Observability hooks added — span tags for fallback_reason, tenant_priority, and selected_variant. Dashboard card drafted in Console (link: https://console.redwood.com/dashboards/fallbacks).
2025-02-20: Preparing PR for runtime changes (RFC #RI-2025-56) and ops playbook; requesting review from Security for KMS audit implications (ticketed).
notes: Trade-offs considered: probabilistic shedding yields better short-term latency distribution but is harder to reason about costs; budgeted-rate chosen to keep unit economics predictable for finance and SRE teams.

Compatibility: fallback will only select hosted variants that are validated for quantization and tokenization equivalence. A compatibility matrix will be checked at selection time; incompatible variants are rejected.
Operational knobs: per-tenant spill budget (tokens/min), region global cap (%), stabilization window (sec), and hazard-mode override for emergency drain.
Open question: whether to charge high-priority tenants for hosted spillover usage or bill from reserved capacity credits — product to decide before GA.
Performance notes: KV cache rehydration latency was a major contributor during POC; we will investigate prefix-sharing heuristics and use early KV-prefetching on spill paths.
Follow-ups: PM to coordinate billing decision (PM-5021), and Design to create Console UX for spill budget adjustments (DES-410).
Ops: Add a synthetic test that periodically induces controlled affinity sheds in staging to validate new metrics and alarms.
